title: TDD inside the agent loop - theater or actual value?
summary: A small exploratory eval finds that asking an agent to do TDD inside its own loop gave no better design, test or mutation scores while costing several times more tokens.

assertions.quote: there was no clearly discernable difference based on TDD workflow versus no TDD workflow
agents still sometimes skipped or faked the red step, or implemented ahead of the test so that it passed immediately

verdicts.note: Consistent with practitioner reports that agents struggle to follow incremental test-first discipline, though evidence is mostly anecdotal.

assertions.quote: TDD reliably cost several times more, how many times exactly is variable.

verdicts.note: More turns and tool calls mechanically raise token usage, though cache hits reduce the dollar impact.

assertions.quote: the non-TDD and test-first runs always created the full design (architecture, data types, edge cases, contracts) before writing any code or tests
tests checked the implementation's output against itself

verdicts.note: A commonly observed failure mode in generated tests, but how often it occurs has not been well quantified.

assertions.quote: They frequently overshot and implemented more than the current test demanded
being overly specific about how we want a model to do something is not a sustainable approach
That feedback should be automated wherever possible
I monitor and improve regression quality with the help of mutation testing, instead of giving elaborate TDD instructions and hoping for the best.

verdicts.note: Mutation testing directly measures test effectiveness, but there is little comparative evidence against TDD prompting.
